routes.reason: Part II of Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups, 53 items. Accepted. The delimitation holds at the pins and in the atlas: IG.3 is 'Branch cycles, rigidity and descent' and IG.5 is 'Hurwitz spaces and function-field branches', and their stage descriptions own Riemann existence, the braid action, field-of-moduli descent, Hurwitz moduli with braid/Nielsen components and tame positive-characteristic covers - not one word about stabilization. A regular-expression sweep of every roadmap extract in the atlas for 'homological stability' returns NOTHING at all, and the only two roadmaps that mention Hurwitz spaces are IG itself and AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry, both of which this route imports rather than replans. So the chain-level machinery of EVW sections 3-6 - the braid-orbit ring R, the graded K-complex, the arc/coset resolution and its spectral sequence, and the central operator U of Lemma 3.5 - has no owner. The proposed id InverseGaloisPartIIHurwitzHomologicalStability is free everywhere in the repository, the title is an exact prefix extension of 'Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups', and 'arithmeticgeometry' is a galaxy id. The brief is honest about its limits in the two places that matter: it fixes the coefficient hypothesis ('field coefficients in which |G| is invertible', which is exactly what makes the spurious scalar of E5 harmless) and it forbids promising 'Frobenius-equivariant stabilization or fixed-q CL convergence', which is precisely the boundary E11 is about.

Source route into InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0, IG.1, IG.3, IG.5, 23 items. Accepted. The four stages exist and are the right owners: IG.0 'Galois categories and fibre functors' and IG.1 'Arithmetic exact sequences and specialization' for the finite-cover image lemmas, IG.3 for the branch-cycle and Riemann-existence input, IG.5 for the Hurwitz-scheme and tame-comparison constructions. The reason keeps the marked/unmarked and tame-family adapters here while importing the general quotient-stack construction from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.4 rather than duplicating it, which is the right division. This is also the route that carries the labelled-family adapter whose stack subtlety the extraction records as E16 in the cited Achter-Pries source, so the design job inherits the warning with the work.

Source route into ArithmeticStatistics ST.0 and ST.5, 46 items. Accepted. ST.0 is 'Families, heights and measures' and ST.5 is 'Beyond first moments', which is exactly where the Cohen-Lenstra moment machinery belongs: Lemma 8.2 (a measure on finite abelian ell-groups is determined by its surjection moments), Proposition 8.3 (moments force distribution) and the generalized-dihedral counting dictionary of Proposition 8.7. The reason is careful not to claim these exist in Lean already. One boundary worth recording for whoever builds these layers: PAPER-BARYSOROKER-KOUKOULOPOULOS-KOZMA-23 proposes a Part II of this same roadmap for random polynomials of growing degree, and the two do not collide - that one owns the growing-degree coefficient-law probability space, this one owns class-group moments in a fixed-genus-free, q-to-infinity limit. They should import each other's conventions, not each other's theorems.

notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, for issue 1185, 23 September 2026. Verdict: accept.

SOURCE. The published Annals PDF was re-fetched and hashes to 6c10d770348c625ad9fe80d2c47093cde2a2ba05f39a28d547743f0f4993a7f6, matching the recorded hash byte for byte; Annals PDFs carry no per-download stamp, so the record is reproducible. 58 pages, printed page = PDF page + 728, confirmed against the running heads. arXiv 0912.0325 ends at the December 2015 version, whose comment reads 'Final version; to appear in Annals of Mathematics', and Crossref's record of doi:10.4007/annals.2016.183.3.1 has an empty relation object with no update-to or updated-by (checked independently on 23 September 2026). A Crossref bibliographic search for an erratum returns none.

MISTAKES. All 19 findings were checked at their locators and all 19 are confirmed. Fourteen concern EVW; five (E15-E17 Achter-Pries, E18-E19 Vasiu) concern cited sources, which is established house practice - PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-22, PAPER-NGODAC-21, PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-TANIGUCHI-ETAL-20 and PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 all record findings in cited works - and their locators name the other document first, so the register entry cannot be misread. Both cited sources were re-fetched and read at the locators.

Seven are settled by the paper against itself, and I report those as decisive: E1 (the sentence says the densities of Theorem 1.2 are 'equal to 1'; Theorem 1.2, three pages earlier, gives a value < 1, and the events for distinct A are disjoint); E2 (the descriptions of Sur and Sur^c are interchanged, against the definition ten lines above); E3 (M tensor R[U] in the sentence, R[U] tensor M in the next display, and M is a left module over a noncommutative ring); E9 (section 8.6's standing hypothesis supplies the missing 'abelian'); E10 (Proposition 8.7 states that (L,alpha) and (L,beta) are isomorphic exactly when beta = +-alpha, so the identification on p.779 drops that quotient); E12 (the basis is y_1,...,y_g, so 'i > g' indexes nothing); E14 (section 8.1 defines the space as isomorphism classes of finite abelian ell-groups, so the whole class group cannot be the invariant). E5 is settled by the paper's own two definitions: U_D and U_Q are both unnormalized sums, so the operator surviving on a monodromy-Q component is U_Q with coefficient 1, not |c|/|c cap Q| times it.

RECOMPUTED. Three witnesses were rebuilt from scratch. E6: enumerating all 48 surjections C9 x C3 ->> C3 x C3, exactly 36 have NO lift along the given enlargement and 12 have lifts - matching both the finding and the extraction's own liftHistogram {0: 36, 9: 12} - while |Sur(X,A')| = |Aut(C9 x C3)| = 108 >= 96 = (ell-1)|Sur(X,A)|, so the aggregate inequality (8.4.1) survives and this is a gap in the proof, not a counterexample to the lemma. E15: in SL_2(Z/9) the subgroup generated by [[0,1],[8,0]] and [[1,7],[6,7]] has order 24 and maps bijectively onto SL_2(F_3), inside a group of order 648, so its preimage in SL_2(Z_3) is a proper closed subgroup with full mod-3 image and the unqualified 'standard group theory argument' fails at (g,ell) = (1,3). E7: with nu_n = (1-ell^-n)mu + ell^-n delta_{(C_ell)^n}, the total variation distance is at most 2 ell^-n while the C_ell moment is 2 - 2 ell^-n, so distribution convergence does not give moment convergence. E17's counterexample I checked by hand: over C(t) the twist y^2 = x^3 - t^2 x has arithmetic image {+-I}, trivial geometric image, and C(t) already contains every root of unity.

THE ONE FINDING THAT REACHES A STATED RESULT is E11, and it is correctly classified. Theorem 1.2 asserts its limit 'as q -> infinity with q != 1 (mod ell)'; nothing before it restricts q - the footnote defines only 'imaginary' - yet section 8.6 opens 'Let ell be an odd prime not dividing q' and Theorem 8.8, which the paper says implies Theorem 1.2, assumes 'ell an odd prime not dividing q or q - 1'. Two cases the printed hypothesis allows are therefore uncovered: q = ell^k, excluded outright by section 8.6, and q even, where the section 8 apparatus (Kummer quadratic extensions K(sqrt f) of odd degree, tame G-covers whose class consists of involutions, and the count |S_n| = 2(q^n - q^(n-1)) taken modulo squares) does not apply. The extraction states this as a supported-domain gap and not as a disproof, which is the right register.

CORRECTIONS MADE IN PLACE. The substantial one: every finding's 'printed' field was replaced by a verbatim quotation of the source. As recorded, ten of the nineteen were single words or bare phrases - 'respectively', 'equivalent', 'indivisible', 'ell-group', 'i>g', 'is an isomorphism', 'the Lie bracket', 'a free R-module', 'principal homogeneous space', 'equal to 1' - and scripts/errata.py prints that field into the public register as 'The source says `...`'. An entry reading 'The source says `respectively`' cannot be checked by a reader who does not have the paper open, and PROTOCOL section 18 asks for 'what the source says, quoted'. Each replacement was read in the published text (E5 and the Lemma 4.6 display on rendered page images, since the text layer mangles them), and what the extraction had recorded is preserved alongside in 'printedAsRecorded'. Second: E12's locator said Proposition 8.9 where the paper says Lemma 8.9. Third: a 'verification' block was added for this review; the extraction's own 'validation', 'audit' and 'completion' blocks are untouched. No item, status, route or locator otherwise changed.

TWO THINGS I DID NOT CHANGE. E7 is classified as affecting the proof; the sentence is expository - it is about the Cohen-Lenstra conjecture over Q, not about the function-field theorem - and no proof in the paper uses the converse implication, so I would have said it reaches no further than the sentence itself. I left the classification and recorded the qualification in the verdict instead. And the unit tests carry kinds 'sanity', 'edge' and 'negative' with an 'expected' field, rather than PROTOCOL section 12's vocabulary and its 'statement' field; section 12 governs blueprint nodes rather than paper items, so this is a note for the design job, not a defect.

ITEMS AND STATUSES. 137 items: 7 library, 8 planned, 122 missing. All seven library declarations were opened at the pinned commits. My own structural checks: 137 unique ids, every missing item routed exactly once, all prerequisites resolve, the prerequisite graph is acyclic, and every missing definition or construction carries an API outline and at least three tests (39 items, 83 API entries, 117 tests).
